In your Warrior I, you’ve got the overall shape, and with a few focused adjustments you’ll feel much more stable and open.

1) **Your spine is not straight**  
Right now your torso is slightly off its tall, neutral line. To improve this, **lift up through the crown of your head** and **lengthen your spine** as if you’re creating space between each vertebra. Gently **draw your ribs in** so you’re not collapsing or over-arching—think “tall and steady” through the center.

2) **Your arms are not straight up**  
Your arms are drifting instead of stacking directly overhead. Bring your arms **straight up beside your ears**, reaching evenly through both hands. Keep the shoulders relaxed—**lift from the sides of your body**, not by scrunching the shoulders. A helpful cue: **biceps frame your ears** while you stay long through your neck.

3) **Your knees are not directly over your ankles**  
Your knee alignment needs a bit more precision for strength and safety. Adjust your stance so your **front knee tracks directly over your front ankle**. You may need to **shorten or lengthen your stance slightly** to make that happen. As you bend the front knee, keep it steady and supported so you feel grounded through the foot.

Take a breath, reset with these three points, and hold the pose again—you’re very close, and these changes will make Warrior I feel stronger and more spacious.
